questions.question: What is the 'cache-aside' pattern?
options: Always read from the database, never the cache
Check the cache first; on a miss, do the expensive work, store the result in the cache, then return it
Cache everything permanently, forever
A pattern only usable with databases, never with computed values
questions.explanation: Cache-aside is exactly this check-then-populate flow: TryGetValue (or GetOrCreateAsync) checks the cache; only on a miss does the real (expensive) work happen, with the result cached for next time.

questions.question: What does `_cache.Set("all_products", products, TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10))` mean?
options: The products are permanently cached
The cached value is automatically evicted after 10 minutes, after which the next request becomes a cache miss again
The database is queried every 10 minutes automatically
It caches for exactly 10 requests, not a time duration
questions.explanation: The TimeSpan argument is an expiration — after that duration elapses, the cached entry is removed, and the next lookup will be a miss requiring fresh work.

questions.question: A CreateProduct method adds a new product to the database but doesn't touch the cache. What's the bug?
options: There is no bug
The cached 'all_products' list is now stale — it won't include the new product until its expiration naturally passes
The new product won't actually save to the database
This causes a runtime exception
questions.explanation: The cache has no way to know the underlying data changed. Without explicitly calling _cache.Remove("all_products") (or otherwise updating the entry), callers will see the stale cached list until it expires on its own.

questions.question: Which scenario is a BAD candidate for caching?
options: A rarely-changing list of countries
A user's current bank account balance, checked right before allowing a withdrawal
A product catalog that updates a few times a day
A computed report that's expensive to generate and rarely changes
questions.explanation: A bank balance needs to be accurate at the moment of a critical decision (allowing a withdrawal) — staleness here could allow overdrawing. This is exactly the kind of data where caching's correctness risk outweighs its performance benefit.

questions.question: What does `GetOrCreateAsync` combine into one call?
options: Nothing, it's identical to Set
The check-cache-then-populate-on-miss flow — check the cache, and only run the provided lambda (and cache its result) if there was a miss
Deleting and recreating the entire cache
It only works for database calls, not any other computation
questions.explanation: GetOrCreateAsync is a convenience wrapper around the exact TryGetValue/Set cache-aside pattern — check first, populate only on a miss, all in one call.

questions.question: Caching per-user data under one shared cache key could cause one user to see another user's data.
questions.explanation: This is a real and serious class of bug — if the cache key doesn't include something that distinguishes users (like a user id), everyone sharing that key would see whichever user's data was cached first.
